A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viral UL97 kinase phosphorylates serine 5 of the RNA polymerases II CTD in vitro and in vivo, and that this modification is important for viral gene expression in vivo.
UL97 is a serine/threonine protein kinase that phosphorylates the RNA polymerase C-terminal domain in vitro, and that this phosphorylation is likely to be a significant part of the viral life cycle.
UL97 is a viral CTD kinase that can phosphorylate serine 5 of the RNA polymerases in vitro but that this is only one of many factors involved in the regulation of the RNA polymerization machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UL97 protein kinase phosphorylates the C-terminal domain (CT) of the RNA polymerases II subunit in human cytomegarovirus-infected human cells.

the UL97 protein kinase phosphorylates the carboxyl-terminal repeat domain (CTD), which is part of the largest sub-unit of RNA polymerase, in vitro, and that this phosphorylation occurs predominantly on the serine 5 of the YSPTSPSP consensus sequence of the CTD.
the UL97 protein kinase phosphorylates the RNA polymerase CTD in vitro.
